source.title: Features of SAEs are universal - but only up to an unknown random rotation

record.tranche_reason: The study reports that high cross-model SAE decoder similarity does not ensure cross-model reconstruction, and argues that the claim of SAE universality needs qualification because transfer requires rotation alignment.
record.gate_note: The study also reports steering-transfer and attribution-patching results. These do not directly measure the listed versions about superposition or SAE features, so they are not included as rows. The structured Gaussian reconstruction is a calibration baseline, not a result on an SAE feature.
record.test_reason: The study measures cross-seed SAE feature similarity and transfer on a toy transformer and on Pythia-70m. It argues that SAE feature universality, the stability and canonicity in V5, holds only up to an orthogonal rotation, so the claim needs restating.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The author adds that feature universality should be defined as equivalence classes under rotation, and that the rotation appears Haar-random.
record.recipe_differences: Measures cross-seed SAE transfer and reconstruction, fits orthogonal Procrustes rotations, and examines rotation statistics; it does not test the original sparse-feature superposition setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Transfer depends strongly on site: the toy's shared input site transfers perfectly while internal sites fail; post-alignment Pythia recovery is weakest immediately before the first transformer block and best in the middle of the stack.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-seed Procrustes rotations have Frobenius distance near sqrt(2d), and their eigenphases are indistinguishable from Haar SO(d) by KS test.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Independently trained same-architecture transformers represent the same function in residual bases related by near-Haar-random rotations.

record.problems: The study itself flags the frontier-scale version as untested. The cross-checkpoint drift result is limited to one layer, one seed, and one checkpoint pair. The author also identifies the Haar-distribution claim as especially deserving scrutiny.
record.rows_left_out: Steering-transfer results in §6 and attribution-patching comparisons in §8 were not extracted because they do not directly measure the listed SAE-feature versions. The structured Gaussian calibration in §3 was also left out because it is a noise baseline rather than an SAE-feature result.

untested.parts: No sparse-feature toy setup, no sparsity transition, no geometry analysis.
No test of capacity or feature importance as the cause of polysemanticity.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemantic neurons.
No SAE self-reconstruction or feature-spread results reported for Pythia, except one 0.907 self-EV at a checkpoint in §7.
Dictionary completeness is not tested. Stability across architectures, datasets, SAE hyperparameters and frontier scale is not tested.
No test of one- versus multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: Cross-checkpoint SAE transfer on Pythia-70m seed 1, layer 3, step 3000 vs 143000: self EV 0.907, raw transfer EV -0.86, post-rotation EV 0.73, ||R−I|| 16.81. This bears on SAE feature stability over training. The author flags it as a single data point.
Structured Gaussian calibration baseline (EV 0.94–0.98). This is the comparison the author uses for raw cross-seed transfer, and should be the baseline for r5 and r6.

record.verdict_notes: Internal tension worth flagging: if residual bases were related by Haar-random rotations, unaligned decoder-column cosines across seeds should be near zero. Reported cosines of 0.89–0.93 suggest an alignment step not described in the post, which matters for reading r1–r3. It is a LessWrong post with an arXiv preprint and is not peer-reviewed. The toy seeds share frozen input/output weights. Steering and attribution-patching results are correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: No test of sparse-feature competition, feature overlap, or a sparsity-dependent transition and geometry.
No test of whether feature importance or limited capacity explains polysemanticity.
No test of alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.
Tests SAE reconstruction on Pythia-70m in the reported cross-seed alignment setting, but does not test feature spread across neurons or establish feature sparsity directly.

Tests cross-seed similarity and reconstruction transfer, including after rotation alignment. Does not establish completeness of the SAE dictionary or stability across other architectures, datasets, or training procedures.
No test of whether represented features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: toy
rows.operation_detail: Applied the seed-0 SAE to activations at the shared input site.

conditions.value: common and bit-identical between coordinated seeds

rows.value: equals the corresponding self-reconstruction EV to four decimals
rows.note: The shared input site is the study's control for the internal-site transfer failure.
rows.check: The author says this result holds 'as it must': the input site is bit-identical across the toy's coordinated seeds. It is a pipeline sanity check, not evidence on feature stability.

rows.subject: toy
rows.operation_detail: Applied seed-0 SAE to another seed's activations without alignment.
rows.note: The post describes the transfer failure as worse than predicting the activation mean.
rows.check: Raw transfer failing is absence of direct transfer, not the opposite effect. The author's comparison point is the structured Gaussian calibration (EV 0.94–0.98), which the record dropped.

rows.subject: Pythia-70m
rows.stage_stated: trained on The Pile; nine independently-trained seeds
rows.operation_detail: Applied seed-0 SAE to other seeds' activations without alignment.

conditions.value: internal layers; every internal layer from the second block onward is negative

rows.note: The range is reported without a per-layer or per-seed breakdown; the post states that every internal layer from the second block onward has negative EV.
rows.check: Same as r5. The range -2.11 to 0.75 has no per-layer breakdown. 'Reversed' overstates it; transfer fails.

rows.subject: toy
rows.operation_detail: Applied seed-0 SAE to another seed's activations after orthogonal Procrustes alignment.
rows.note: The post says recovery is uniform across the toy interior.
rows.check: This is a toy-model result, so it cannot bear on V4, which concerns LLMs. Cross-seed aligned transfer is evidence on feature stability (V5), not on whether sparse features exist.

rows.subject: Pythia-70m
rows.stage_stated: trained on The Pile; nine independently-trained seeds
rows.operation_detail: Applied seed-0 SAE to another seed's activations after orthogonal Procrustes alignment.

conditions.value: sites; best results in the middle of the stack and worst immediately before the first transformer block

rows.note: Alignment substantially restores reconstruction; the reported range includes a weaker pre-first-block site.
rows.check: Cross-seed aligned transfer does not test whether LLMs contain SAE-recoverable sparse features, so the V4 link is removed. Partial because the pre-first-block site reaches only about 0.85.

relationships.condition: Cross-seed decoder similarity and post-Procrustes transfer, toy and Pythia-70m
relationships.reason: Mean max-cosine is 0.89 (toy) and 0.91–0.93 (Pythia), with about 98% of features matching above 0.5 (r1, r2, r3). Aligned transfer EV is 0.976–0.990 on the toy (r7).
relationships.display_finding: Mean max-cosine was 0.89 on the toy and 0.91–0.93 on Pythia, with about 98% of features matching above 0.5, and aligned transfer explained 0.976–0.990 of variance on the toy.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Cross-seed decoder similarity and post-Procrustes transfer, toy and Pythia-70m
source_check.reason: r1–r3 show strong decoder matching; r7 shows near-complete toy reconstruction after alignment. This supports stability under the stated alignment condition, without establishing completeness.

relationships.condition: Direct cross-seed SAE application at internal sites without alignment
relationships.reason: A seed-0 SAE gives negative EV on other seeds: -6.56 worst case on the toy, -2.11 to 0.75 on Pythia (r5, r6). Features are equivalent only up to a rotation.
relationships.display_finding: A seed-0 SAE transferred poorly to other seeds, with explained variance as low as -6.56 on the toy and -2.11 to 0.75 on Pythia, so features were equivalent only up to a rotation.

source_check.reason: r5–r6 and §3 explicitly establish absent direct transfer at the specified internal sites, with negative EV. Under the verdict rules, absence in this condition group challenges V5; recovery after alignment belongs to a separate group.

relationships.reason: Aligned EV is 0.85–0.99, weakest immediately before the first transformer block (r8).
relationships.display_finding: After alignment, explained variance reached 0.85–0.99, weakest just before the first transformer block.

source_check.label: limits_scope
